cost_basis.cheapest_design: Decided 3 requires a ruling to pass the World Builder's existing rules check. The model rules review is not a pass mark: it returns findings only and a build goes on without it when it fails (scripts/review_rules.py:1-7), so Decided 3 does not require it for judge rulings; the required part is the free declaration check and test run. Cheaper option recorded: drop the model review for judge rulings, about $0.05 per run instead of $0.54 (interpreter $0.009 + judge $0.043). Chosen: keep the review (inferred by agent, 2026-11-09). Reason: the sawmill case showed the free checks pass a valid but wrong rule (evidence/ai-judge/plain-baseline/sawmill-test-run.json), and the review is the one existing step that reads a rule against the world's description; $0.49 per run is small next to a wrong rule installed for everyone. J2 runs the review on the saved sawmill rule and drops it if it does not flag the single price. The plain version (one judge call per attempt, no test run before install) would save only the confirm call (about $0.02 per run) and installs malformed or wrong rules. The judge is called only for an attempt no rule covers, each ruling becomes a rule so the same attempt never calls it again, and it uses the interpreter's cheap model and route. Total about $0.54 per run with 10 rulings, most of it the rules review. Stopping point (J5): asking every round costs about $0.07 per 46-round run; the chosen cheaper trigger asks only after a round that changed a field people's moves can change (docs/plans/ai_judge.md, Stopping point).

cases.case: sawmill offers to pay the logger for 3 cedar logs
cases.finding: Today's built path recorded the attempt as unmatched and changed nothing. The plain ruling read every value right, named the logger's choice and found a real gap (saw-slats cannot saw logs the sawmill holds). Its rule passed the rules check but is wrong twice: it charges one price for 3 logs (the language has no multiplication), and it moves the logger's logs on the sawmill's move alone, with no agreement from the logger, although its own ruling called the sale the logger's choice: a failure against Decided 4. The existing scripted test run did not catch the price (it tried 1-log purchases only), and a 3-log attempt was accepted, moving 3 logs for 10 coins instead of 30 (evidence/ai-judge/plain-baseline/sawmill-test-run.json).

cases.case: shop offers the pencil factory $1,000 for pencils
cases.finding: Today's built path recorded it as unmatched and changed nothing. The plain ruling named the factory's choice correctly, but its rule had no effects and was rejected by the rules check (participants must exactly name entity_ref fields).

Today's built path recorded it as unmatched and changed nothing. The plain ruling allowed the pickup (the tray is on the counter, so a general move for a waiter to pick up an empty tray from a surface fits) and named the blocker the engine's own checks name (the carry move needs the tray held by the waiter; it is on the counter). Its rule was rejected by the rules check only for its field name ('from' is not an identifier).

plain_baseline.verdict: The plain version reads the world correctly at these sizes, so the judge's input starts from it (the whole world). It is not enough on its own. Shown: the declaration check stops malformed rules (2 of 3 rejected, rules-check.json). Not shown: that pass 2 stops a wrong but valid rule; the accepted sawmill rule passed the declaration check and the scripted test run (sawmill-test-run.json), so those checks catch malformed rules only, and whether the judge's reading of the test-run report and its one revision catch such a rule is untested until J2. Pass 1 (discover for the person acting and each person named, plus the named entities' values) showed no added value here and is kept only because it costs no call.

stage_effects.stage: pass 2, declaration check: the rules check of the proposed rule before it is installed (J1, J3)
stage_effects.gap: malformed rules: 2 of 3 plain-version rules were rejected; without this check they would be installed and fail

stage_effects.stage: pass 2, test run: a proposed rule run on a copy of the world, its report read by the judge before install (J1, J2)
stage_effects.gap: a valid but wrong rule (the sawmill rule charges one price for 3 logs and moves logs without the logger's agreement). The existing scripted test run tried only 1-log purchases and flagged nothing; a direct 3-log attempt was accepted, 3 logs for 10 coins. So no deterministic check catches it; whether the judge catches it from the report is untested

stage_effects.stage: one revision after the test run (J2)
stage_effects.gap: a rejected or wrong rule from the first proposal (all 3 in the plain baseline) gets one more try before the attempt is refused as a language gap

stage_effects.stage: pass 1: engine.discover for the person acting and each person the attempt names, plus the named entities' current values, given to the judge (J1)
stage_effects.gap: on worlds too large to read whole, the judge could miss a blocker an installed rule already names for another person involved (Rosa's sign-release blocker is on her page, not Vik's); at today's sizes the plain version read the facts right, so the effect is not shown
